issues.problem: SIGN_IN treats any error containing authoriz/authoris as a sign-in failure. Authorization failures can mean the signed-in account lacks access to a vault or item. This also contradicts the guide's claim that the hint appears only for errors about signing in.
issues.suggested_fix: Restrict detection to known authentication/session phrases such as 'not currently signed in', 'sign in', 'unlock', 'locked'; remove the broad authori[sz] alternative and add a test confirming an authorization-denied error gets no sign-in hint.
issues.failure_scenario: A signed-in user without permission receives 'not authorized'; cookwright wrongly recommends op signin or unlocking the app, obscuring the real access-control problem. Tests cover signed-out and missing-vault errors but not authorization denial.
issues.evidence: onepassword.mjs:49 SIGN_IN includes authori[sz]; used at :124-126 to pass signIn to messages.mjs:871-872, which then adds 'sign in ... unlock the 1Password app'. A 'not authorized' access-denial line matches and gets the wrong hint. I could not confirm op's exact wording for such errors. Tests are not shown to cover it.

issues.problem: The sign-in hint is now given only when op's first stderr line matches /sign(ed)?[ -]?in|unlock|locked|authori[sz]/i. Before this change the hint was always given. The regex misses sign-in failures that op words differently, and it also runs over the vault and item names that op quotes in the same line.
issues.suggested_fix: Test the regex only against op's message after the `[ERROR] <date> <time>` prefix, with any quoted names removed. Also match the account and desktop-integration phrasings ('no accounts configured', 'connecting to desktop app', 'logged in'). Or keep the hint unconditional and append it after op's line, so a missed match only adds noise rather than losing guidance.
issues.failure_scenario: Case 1, the hint is lost. A developer whose op has no account configured, or whose 1Password app has CLI integration turned off, gets op's line ('No accounts configured for use with 1Password CLI', or 'connecting to desktop app: … make sure … Integrate with 1Password CLI'). Neither phrase matches, so the refusal drops the 'op signin, or unlock the 1Password app' hint that it printed before this change. Case 2, a wrong hint. A template references a vault named 'Locked Keys' that does not exist. op's line `"Locked Keys" isn't a vault in this account` matches 'locked', so the refusal tells the developer to sign in although they are signed in.
issues.evidence: onepassword.mjs:49 regex is tested against the whole first line (:124-125), vault and item names included. A line like `"Locked Keys" isn't a vault in this account` matches /locked/i, so the sign-in hint is wrongly added (messages.mjs:872). 'No accounts configured...' and 'make sure ... Integrate with 1Password CLI' match none of sign-in, unlock, locked or authori[sz], so the hint is dropped. That differs from the always-on hint before the change (qa/round-2.md:22).

issues.problem: The header says the reference file is 'removed whatever happens'. Removal only runs in a JS finally. `run` installs its SIGINT handler only once the child has started, so an interrupt while op is still running kills node before the finally runs and the directory stays behind. The file holds only op:// references, not values, so this is a claim wider than the code rather than a leak. The guide's wording ('removed as soon as op returns, whether it succeeded or not') is accurate. Related wording issue: the guide also calls the file's contents 'the lines already committed in the template', but run accepts an uncommitted template (the banner only flags it), so the lines may not be committed yet.
issues.suggested_fix: Narrow the comment to 'removed when op returns or fails'. Optionally, say in the guide that the references come from the template, without claiming they are committed.
issues.failure_scenario: The developer runs `npx cookwright run dev -- true` with the 1Password backend. op waits on the 1Password app's authorization prompt (the call is capped at 120 s), and the developer presses Ctrl-C. No SIGINT handler is installed yet, so node exits on the default action and the finally never runs. `$TMPDIR/cookwright-op-XXXXXX/references.tpl` (mode 600, references only) stays on disk.
issues.evidence: onepassword.mjs:15-19 header says 'removed whatever happens', but withReferenceFile (about :100-110) removes the directory only in a JS finally. The capture call is synchronous, and engine.mjs:316-337 installs SIGINT handlers only while the child runs. A Ctrl-C during op inject kills node by default and the finally never runs. docs/guides/secrets.md:180 says 'the lines already committed in the template', although run accepts an uncommitted template, so that wording is also loose. The leftover file holds references only, so the severity is P3.
